newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean parliament passes controversial laws.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean parliament passes controversial laws.

text.p: South Korea's ruling party rammed two controversial laws through parliament on Thursday, one revising labour legislation and the other strengthening the powers of the domestic intelligence agency, state media reported.
Opposition members of the National Assembly were not present when the laws were passed by 154 members of the New Korea Party at a special session that began at around dawn.

The state-run Korea Broadcasting System said opposition parties, including the National Congress for New Politics, were insisting the ruling party had acted unconstitutionally and were refusing to accept the validity of the laws.

Labour unions have threatened general strikes if parliament passed the new labour law, which challenges near-total job security by giving employers the right to lay off workers and introduce flexible working hours.
The other law gives wide powers to the National Security Planning Agency to investigate people suspected of sympathising with communist North Korea.

South Korea's version of the U.S. Central Intelligency Agency (CIA) had been stripped of many of its investigative powers by President Kim Young-sam under an election pledge to curb the agency that once hounded the political opposition under military-backed rule.
